transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Good morning, how can I help you?

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Hello. I've just moved to the city to start a new job, and I'd like to open a bank account.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Of course. Are you interested in a current account or a savings account?

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: A current account first. I need something for my salary and bills.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: We have two types. The standard account has no monthly fee, but you pay a small charge if you go overdrawn. The premium account costs five pounds a month, and it includes travel insurance and a larger overdraft.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: I travel a lot for work, so the premium might be worth it. What does the travel insurance cover?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: It covers medical costs abroad and lost luggage, up to a limit of two thousand pounds, but it doesn't cover pre-existing medical conditions.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: I see. I'll think about that. What do I need to open the account?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Two documents: proof of identity, such as a passport, and proof of address. A utility bill is usually accepted, but since you've just moved, you can bring a letter from your employer or your tenancy agreement.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: I have my tenancy agreement with me, but it's in my other bag in the car. Can I come back this afternoon?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Certainly. We're open until four. Alternatively, you could start the application online and upload a photo of the documents.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That's convenient. How long does it take until I can use the account?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Usually about a week. You'll receive a debit card in the post, and your PIN comes separately a day later, for security.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Does the bank have a mobile app?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Yes, and it's quite good. You can check your balance, transfer money and freeze your card if you lose it. Notifications tell you when money comes in or goes out.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That's useful. And what about savings?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Our online saver pays three per cent interest, though the rate can change, and you can withdraw money at any time. There's also a fixed account at four point two per cent for twelve months, but you can't touch the money until the end.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: I'll look at savings later; I'd prefer to settle in first. One more thing: I'd like to send money to my family abroad every month. Are there charges?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: For international transfers, we charge a flat fee of three pounds if you use the app, or ten pounds at a branch. The exchange rate is the market rate plus a margin of one per cent.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: The app, then. Thank you, you've been very helpful.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Not at all. If you decide on the premium account, mention it when you come back, and I'll arrange everything.
